text:
mike_infra: Heads-up — ~30 GPU nodes in us-west2 flipped to NotReady/NoSchedule after the midnight node image roll. Symptoms: kubelet OOMs, device-plugin failing to bind /var/run/nvidia-device-plugin.sock, autoscaler held scaling. Anyone seeing this?

sasha: :eyes: seeing it on the dashboards too. Which nodepool?

mike_infra: us-west2-gpu-preemptible-3 (recent image v2026-02-14). Sample kubectl: 
```
$ kubectl get nodes | grep -i gpu | grep NotReady
gpu-node-02    NotReady,NoSchedule   45m
gpu-node-03    NotReady,NoSchedule   44m
...
```

mike_infra: kubectl describe shows kubelet OOMKilled and device plugin crashloops: 
```
Warning  Failed     5m (x12 over 45m)  kubelet, gpu-node-02  Killed container with id docker://nvidia-device-plugin: oomkill
ContainersReady False (containers with unready status: nvidia-device-plugin)
```

kai: I pulled kubelet logs — saw frequent out-of-memory messages around 03:12 UTC plus repeated attempts to bind socket: 
```
E0324 03:12:21.123456  1234 plugin.go:201] failed to start device plugin: bind /var/run/nvidia-device-plugin.sock: address already in use
fatal error: runtime: out of memory
```

mike_infra: The bind address in-use looks like a leftover socket from previous plugin process. But oom implies kubelet or plugin memory leak during init. Not seeing this on non-gpu pools.

infra-bot: autoscaler: Cluster Autoscaler paused scaling for asg/us-west2-gpu-preemptible-3 due to max-node-provisioning-failure(30).

ops-oncall: This is blocking a set of batch jobs queued for hours. Cost and SLO impact brewing. Can we temporarily unpause autoscaler to force replacement?

sasha: If autoscaler replaces nodes while underlying image causes startup OOM, we'll create more NotReady nodes. Need to mitigate at image level or prevent device-plugin from starting until stable driver ready.

kai: Quick triage steps I ran: 1) SSH into a troubled node, checked dmesg — seeing repeated PCI resets for GPU: 
```
[  412.345678] NVRM: GPU 0000:01:00.0: RmInitAdapter failed! (0x32e0)
[  412.345679] nvidia: probe of 0000:01:00.0 failed with error -22
```
2) Container runtime logs show nvidia-container-runtime complaining about driver version mismatch with kernel modules.

mike_infra: So likely the image includes a newer driver or kernel that doesn't match the NV lib we ship in the init container. The device-plugin tries to allocate shared mem/socket then OOMs if repeatedly crashing.

ops-oncall: Proposal: immediately cordon the pool and scale up a fallback pool with older image to absorb workload. Also pause autoscaler to avoid churn.

sasha: Agreed. Steps: 
- cordon us-west2-gpu-preemptible-3 (prevent new pods)
- set cluster-autoscaler pause for that ASG
- create temporary nodepool us-west2-gpu-fallback with last-known-good image v2026-01-28 and prewarm with 10 nodes
- add taint tolerations as needed for batch jobs

mike_infra: I'm oncordoning now and raising the image rollback PR. Executing: `kubectl cordon -l nodepool=us-west2-gpu-preemptible-3`

infra-bot: action: nodegroup us-west2-gpu-preemptible-3 cordoned by mike_infra

kai: I'm collecting full diagnostics (kubectl describe, kubelet logs, dmesg, /var/log/messages) and will upload to the infra bucket: gs://redwood-infra/diag/2130001111/

ops-oncall: Thanks. Also ping infra-sre@redwood if we need manual kernel/driver rebuilds on image. This will affect Dedicated customers if it lands in prod.

sasha: Quick mitigation note — we can modify the device-plugin DaemonSet to add an initContainer that checks for stable GPU presence before starting and avoids repeated bind attempts: `init: test -S /dev/nvidiactl || exit 1` and exponential backoff in main loop. But that's a stopgap.

mike_infra: For now I've paused autoscaler on the ASG and started the fallback nodepool. New nodes are registering with expected image v2026-01-28. Job backlog should drain to fallback pool.

infra-bot: autoscaler: paused asg/us-west2-gpu-preemptible-3 by mike_infra

ops-oncall: :thumbsup: monitor cost impact and let finance know preemptible fallback will briefly increase charges.

kai: Filing an incident-run doc with steps and root-cause hypothesis (driver/kernel mismatch + device-plugin socket race causing OOM) — will attach traces.

mike_infra: Action items: 1) rollback image for pool (mike_infra) 2) patch device-plugin with init check/backoff (sasha) 3) add kubelet OOM alerting for gpu pools (kai) 4) postmortem + customer comms if Dedicated impacted (ops-oncall).

sasha: ETA for plugin patch ~2 hours, can ship as a canary to us-west2-gpu-fallback first.

ops-oncall: I'll keep autoscaler paused until we confirm stable start on fallback nodes. If any of you need escalation to kernel team, ping me.

mike_infra: I'll update this thread as we see nodes stabilize. Current status: fallback nodes up, approx 7/10 ready and accepting pods. Old pool still shows ~28 NotReady.

kai: Upload complete: diagnostics in gs://redwood-infra/diag/2130001111/ksnaps.tar.gz

sasha: starting plugin patch now, will post PR link once available.

mike_infra: Great. Thanks all — this one looks like a dangerous image-driver combo edge-case. Will follow up with a short postmortem tomorrow. :coffee:
